hyperedges.label: 3D layer handoff choreography across the act timeline
NaN / non-finite containment at input boundaries
Degenerate-input fallback to a safe documented default

nodes.label: describe: backtestLongOnly
nodes.rationale: Equity-curve accounting for long-only signal backtests; the suite exists because multi-bar holds were compounded twice.

nodes.label: multi-bar +10% trade returns +10%
nodes.rationale: Regression: a multi-bar hold that gained 10% reported 18.8% because per-bar returns were double counted into the equity curve.

nodes.label: one-bar trade unchanged
nodes.rationale: Pins that the double-counting fix did not regress the single-bar case, which was already correct under the old formula.

nodes.label: multi-bar loss is exact
nodes.rationale: Losses must be exact too, not just gains — the double-count bug distorted drawdowns in the same way it inflated wins.

nodes.label: two sequential trades compound correctly
nodes.rationale: Guards that consecutive round-trips multiply (1.10*1.20) rather than accumulating extra bars of return between exits and re-entries.

nodes.label: still counts trades and win rate at trade level
nodes.rationale: The equity fix must not turn per-bar bookkeeping into per-bar trade counts: a 3-bar hold is still one trade.
nodes.norm_label: still counts trades and win rate at trade level

nodes.label: acts cover [0,1] contiguously in ACT_ORDER
nodes.rationale: A gap or overlap between consecutive act windows leaves a scroll position with no owning act, so the cinema renders nothing (black frame) at that progress value.

nodes.label: every act has positive width
nodes.rationale: A zero- or negative-width act would be unreachable by scroll and would break the contiguity arithmetic.

nodes.label: copy beats have unique ids and windows inside [0,1]
nodes.rationale: Duplicate beat ids collide on lookup and a window escaping [0,1] is unreachable scroll territory, so the copy never shows.
nodes.norm_label: copy beats have unique ids and windows inside [0,1]

nodes.label: each copy beat sits within some act window
nodes.rationale: A beat spanning an act boundary shows its copy over the wrong visual layer as the acts crossfade.
nodes.norm_label: each copy beat sits within some act window

nodes.label: clamp01 clamps and neutralizes non-finite input
nodes.rationale: NaN and Infinity must collapse to 0 rather than propagate: a NaN opacity makes the whole layer vanish or flicker unpredictably in the compositor.
nodes.norm_label: clamp01 clamps and neutralizes non-finite input

nodes.label: beatOpacity is 0 outside the window (inclusive edges)
nodes.rationale: Pins exact edge semantics: at from and at to the beat is already fully transparent, so adjacent beats never double-render at a shared boundary.
nodes.norm_label: beatopacity is 0 outside the window (inclusive edges)

nodes.label: beatOpacity ramps over the fade width and plateaus at 1
nodes.rationale: The fade must be a trapezoid — linear in, flat hold, linear out — not a triangle that never reaches full opacity.
nodes.norm_label: beatopacity ramps over the fade width and plateaus at 1

nodes.label: flashOpacity is a faint triangle over the start of the matrix act
nodes.rationale: The flash must be strictly confined to [0.84, 0.904] and zero at both edges and at scroll end, or a stray white frame leaks into unrelated acts.
nodes.norm_label: flashopacity is a faint triangle over the start of the matrix act

nodes.label: canvasOpacity holds 1 almost to the end, then a short crossfade to 0
nodes.rationale: The canvas must stay fully opaque through 0.998 and only dissolve in the last 0.002 of scroll, otherwise the cinema fades out early and exposes the page underneath.
nodes.norm_label: canvasopacity holds 1 almost to the end, then a short crossfade to 0

nodes.label: bull3dOpacity is 0 outside the bull window
nodes.rationale: The expensive 3D bull layer must be fully transparent at scroll 0 and 1 so it is never mounted-visible outside its act.
nodes.norm_label: bull3dopacity is 0 outside the bull window

nodes.label: bull3dOpacity fades in, holds opaque, then dissolves out
nodes.rationale: Pins the four-point in0/in1/out0/out1 envelope so the hold segment is genuinely flat at 1 rather than peaking momentarily.
nodes.norm_label: bull3dopacity fades in, holds opaque, then dissolves out

nodes.label: bull3d hands off cleanly: monotonic window, gone before the homepage resolve
nodes.rationale: The 2D matrix rain starts mid-bull-act (~0.796) so the 3D fade-out overlaps it; the bull must be fully gone by ~0.86 when the homepage resolves, keeping the cinema tail purely 2D.
nodes.norm_label: bull3d hands off cleanly: monotonic window, gone before the homepage resolve

nodes.label: dive3dOpacity is 0 outside the tunnel window and 1 through its hold
nodes.rationale: The tunnel must be absent at 0.1 and 0.3 and fully opaque mid-tunnel at 0.19, pinning the envelope shape against drift in the DIVE3D constants.
nodes.norm_label: dive3dopacity is 0 outside the tunnel window and 1 through its hold

nodes.label: dive3d spans the dive act and clears before the regime chart needs the frame
nodes.rationale: Two 3D layers competing for the same frame drops the scene below its frame budget; the dive must vacate before the regime act starts.
nodes.norm_label: dive3d spans the dive act and clears before the regime chart needs the frame

nodes.label: candle3dOpacity is 0 outside the candle window
nodes.rationale: The sample point moved from 0.605 to 0.61 because the ice-lab beat widened the tail; the test pins that the widened window still terminates.
nodes.norm_label: candle3dopacity is 0 outside the candle window

nodes.label: candle3dOpacity holds opaque through the foresight beats
nodes.rationale: The foresight (0.44) and vindication (0.52) copy beats must land on a fully opaque candle layer, not mid-crossfade.
nodes.norm_label: candle3dopacity holds opaque through the foresight beats

nodes.label: candle3d clears before the next act's copy
nodes.rationale: The ice-lab beat deliberately lets the 3D layer spill past ACTS.candle.to as a crossfade to avoid a black flash into safety; the old 'must end by ACTS.candle.to' invariant was replaced by two weaker ones — gone before the safety COPY beat, and the spill capped at 0.02.
nodes.norm_label: candle3d clears before the next act's copy

nodes.label: describe: strategy detector
nodes.rationale: Classifies an arbitrary Leg[] into a named options structure with bias, defined-risk and debit/credit metadata.

nodes.label: flags naked short call as unbounded
nodes.rationale: A naked short call has theoretically infinite loss; defined must be false so the UI can refuse to present it as risk-capped.
nodes.norm_label: flags naked short call as unbounded

nodes.label: detects bull call spread
nodes.rationale: Pins that long-low/short-high calls classify as a bullish, defined-risk debit — the ordering that generateStrategies must emit.

nodes.label: detects bull put spread
nodes.rationale: Long-low/short-high puts are a bullish credit structure, distinguishing net credit from the debit call spread with the same directional bias.

nodes.label: detects long straddle (same strike, long both)
nodes.rationale: Same-strike long call plus long put must read as volatile bias, not directional.
nodes.norm_label: detects long straddle (same strike, long both)

nodes.label: detects long strangle (different strikes, long both)
nodes.rationale: Strike inequality is the only thing separating a strangle from a straddle; the detector must not collapse the two.
nodes.norm_label: detects long strangle (different strikes, long both)

nodes.label: detects iron condor (4 legs, condor shape)
nodes.rationale: Recognises the Klp<Ksp<Ksc<Klc wing ordering as a neutral defined-risk structure.
nodes.norm_label: detects iron condor (4 legs, condor shape)

nodes.label: detects iron butterfly when middle strikes coincide
nodes.rationale: Collapsing the two short strikes onto one point turns a condor into a butterfly; the shape test must branch on that equality.
nodes.norm_label: detects iron butterfly when middle strikes coincide

nodes.label: falls back to Custom for unknown shape
nodes.rationale: An unrecognised three-leg combination must degrade to Custom rather than being force-fitted into the nearest named strategy.
nodes.norm_label: falls back to custom for unknown shape

nodes.label: describe: deriveMarketState
nodes.rationale: Derives PRE/REGULAR/POST/CLOSED from Yahoo-shaped currentTradingPeriod metadata plus a wall-clock epoch.

nodes.label: CLOSED overnight/weekend
nodes.rationale: The headline bug: overnight and weekend timestamps used to report REGULAR, so the UI claimed the market was live when it had been shut for hours.

nodes.label: CLOSED before the pre session opens
nodes.rationale: Guards the other side of the day: a timestamp earlier than pre.start must not fall through into any open session.
nodes.norm_label: closed before the pre session opens

nodes.label: boundary: regular end is no longer REGULAR
nodes.rationale: Off-by-one at the session edge: the exact regular.end epoch is also post.start and must resolve to POST, so the interval test is half-open, not inclusive.
nodes.norm_label: boundary: regular end is no longer regular

nodes.label: honours an explicit provider state when present
nodes.rationale: When the upstream feed states marketState directly it wins over local period arithmetic, even where the two disagree.
nodes.norm_label: honours an explicit provider state when present

nodes.label: no trading periods: recent trade => REGULAR, stale => CLOSED
nodes.rationale: With no currentTradingPeriod the function falls back to trade recency; a 60s-old print reads REGULAR while a 2h-old print reads CLOSED, so missing metadata never pins the UI to a stale live state.
nodes.norm_label: no trading periods: recent trade => regular, stale => closed

nodes.label: empty meta never throws
nodes.rationale: Wholly undefined metadata must degrade to CLOSED rather than raising, so a failed upstream fetch cannot crash the render.

nodes.label: describe: splitLayers
nodes.rationale: Partitions hero headline lines into layers rendered behind and in front of the 3D subject.

nodes.label: splits lines into behind/front by the marker index
nodes.rationale: The marker index is exclusive on the behind side; getting it off by one puts a headline line on the wrong side of the subject.
nodes.norm_label: splits lines into behind/front by the marker index

nodes.label: clamps out-of-range markers
nodes.rationale: A marker beyond the line count or at 0 must yield an empty partition instead of an undefined slice — an out-of-range index must not produce holes in the rendered copy.

nodes.label: describe: buildColumns
nodes.rationale: Generates the per-column phase/speed table driving the particle curtain animation.

nodes.label: buildColumns is deterministic for a given seed
nodes.rationale: The column table must come from a seeded PRNG, not Math.random: non-determinism means server and client render different curtains and React hydration mismatches.
nodes.norm_label: buildcolumns is deterministic for a given seed

nodes.label: keeps phase and speed in sane ranges
nodes.rationale: phase must stay in [0,1) and speed in (0.2, 1.61); a zero or negative speed freezes or reverses a column and a phase outside the unit interval desynchronises the wrap.
nodes.norm_label: keeps phase and speed in sane ranges

nodes.label: series() deterministic GBM-ish fixture
nodes.rationale: A seeded xorshift-style PRNG produces a reproducible random-walk price path so distributional assertions about hurst are stable across runs.

nodes.label: trending() momentum-persistent fixture
nodes.rationale: An AR(1) momentum path (m = 0.85m + noise) exists to prove the estimator discriminates regimes rather than merely staying in range.

nodes.label: reverting() mean-reverting fixture
nodes.rationale: An Ornstein-Uhlenbeck-style pull toward 100 provides the low-H counterpart to the trending fixture.

nodes.label: describe: hurst
nodes.rationale: Hurst exponent estimator classifying a price series as TREND / RANDOM / REVERT; rewritten to Anis-Lloyd-corrected R/S after the lag-std estimator proved unusable.

nodes.label: hurst stays in [0,1] across the bar counts that used to blow up
nodes.rationale: Lag 64 used to be admitted at 65 samples, leaving a 1-element difference series; std() then returned 0 and log(1e-9) = -20.7 dominated the regression slope, throwing H far outside [0,1]. Sweeps n=33..200 for finiteness and range.
nodes.norm_label: hurst stays in [0,1] across the bar counts that used to blow up

nodes.label: no longer returns the -6.59 outlier at the 65/66-bar boundary
nodes.rationale: Pins the exact bar counts (65 and 66) where the degenerate-lag bug produced a concrete H of -6.59.
nodes.norm_label: no longer returns the -6.59 outlier at the 65/66-bar boundary

nodes.label: centres a random walk near 0.5 instead of the old ~0.19
nodes.rationale: The lag-std estimator was biased so low (~0.19) that a random walk always read REVERT; raw R/S is biased the other way (~0.60), hence the Anis-Lloyd correction. Median over 40 seeds must land in (0.4, 0.6).
nodes.norm_label: centres a random walk near 0.5 instead of the old ~0.19

nodes.label: separates trending from mean-reverting regimes
nodes.rationale: Being correctly centred is not enough — the estimator must also order trend > walk > revert and clear the documented 0.55 / 0.45 decision thresholds.

nodes.label: the documented RANDOM regime is actually reachable
nodes.rationale: The old estimator never once produced 0.45 <= H <= 0.55 on a random walk, so the RANDOM label documented in the UI was dead code; at least 5 of 40 seeds must now land in the band.
nodes.norm_label: the documented random regime is actually reachable

nodes.label: hurst falls back to 0.5 on degenerate input
nodes.rationale: Too few bars (31), zero dispersion everywhere (80 identical prices) and a 3-element series must all return the neutral 0.5 rather than a spurious regime call.
nodes.norm_label: hurst falls back to 0.5 on degenerate input

nodes.label: describe: macd
nodes.rationale: MACD line / signal / histogram, reworked after the signal was seeded from zero and fabricated a crossover on the first bar.

nodes.label: keeps the signal null until it has 9 real line values
nodes.rationale: The 9-period EMA seed needs 9 real samples, so the signal must start exactly 8 bars after the first line value rather than emitting early half-formed numbers.
nodes.norm_label: keeps the signal null until it has 9 real line values

nodes.label: does not emit the fabricated first-bar crossover
nodes.rationale: Old behaviour seeded sig = line*k exactly, so histogram = (1-k)*line and always shared the line's sign — manufacturing a guaranteed crossover signal on the very first bar. The histogram must be null there instead.
nodes.norm_label: does not emit the fabricated first-bar crossover

nodes.label: seeds the signal from real data — signal tracks the line, not zero
nodes.rationale: A properly seeded SMA sits within the local range of the line; the zero-seeded version started at ~20% of it, so the first real signal value was meaningless.
nodes.norm_label: seeds the signal from real data — signal tracks the line, not zero

nodes.label: histogram is null wherever either input is null
nodes.rationale: Absence must propagate through the subtraction rather than coercing a null operand to 0 and producing a phantom bar.
nodes.norm_label: histogram is null wherever either input is null

nodes.label: describe: sortino
nodes.rationale: Annualised Sortino ratio; the denominator was computing the wrong downside deviation and the no-downside guard returned the worst possible score.

nodes.label: matches hand-computed downside deviation
nodes.rationale: The ratio was 3.58x overstated — the old formula returned 39.69 where the hand-computed value is under 15, because downside deviation divided by the count of negative returns instead of the full sample.

nodes.label: reports unbounded, not 0, when there is no downside
nodes.rationale: std([]) was 0 so the divide-by-zero guard returned 0 — the WORST score for the BEST case, an all-positive return series. Must be Infinity instead.
nodes.norm_label: reports unbounded, not 0, when there is no downside

nodes.label: honours the target return rf in the denominator
nodes.rationale: rf is a target return, not just a numerator offset: returns below it become shortfalls and must raise the downside deviation.
nodes.norm_label: honours the target return rf in the denominator

nodes.label: sortino is 0 for an empty series
nodes.rationale: Distinguishes the genuinely empty case (0) from the no-downside case (Infinity), which the old shared guard conflated.
nodes.norm_label: sortino is 0 for an empty series

nodes.label: describe: probBS input clamping
nodes.rationale: Black-Scholes probability that spot finishes inside a price band, hardened against non-positive band edges that make log() undefined.

nodes.label: probBS never returns NaN for a non-positive band
nodes.rationale: Bands with negative or zero edges (-50..120, -200..-100, 0..120, +/-1e6) feed log() a non-positive argument; the result must clamp into [0,1] instead of returning NaN to the UI.
nodes.norm_label: probbs never returns nan for a non-positive band

nodes.label: still prices a normal band sensibly
nodes.rationale: Guards that the clamping hardening did not flatten legitimate bands to a degenerate 0 or 1.
nodes.norm_label: still prices a normal band sensibly

nodes.label: describe: strategy strikes stay positive and finite
nodes.norm_label: describe: strategy strikes stay positive and finite

nodes.label: every band yields finite money on every strategy card
nodes.rationale: A dragged band could go negative and every strategy card then rendered $NaN; parametrised over four bands including fully-negative (-120..-80) and sub-dollar (0.1..0.2) to assert positive strikes and finite premium/cost/maxLoss/maxProfit.
nodes.norm_label: every band yields finite money on every strategy card

nodes.label: describe: safety + kill switch
nodes.rationale: Risk-guardrail store plus the paper-trading ledger it polices; state is reset in beforeEach because both are module-level singletons.

nodes.label: training wheels are on by default
nodes.rationale: The safe default must be opt-out, not opt-in: a fresh user starts with guardrails engaged.
nodes.norm_label: training wheels are on by default

nodes.label: trigger fires when realized loss exceeds limit
nodes.rationale: The kill switch must latch and retain a human-readable reason naming the breached limit, so the block can be explained to the user.
nodes.norm_label: trigger fires when realized loss exceeds limit

nodes.label: setDailyLossLimit clamps negatives to 0
nodes.rationale: A negative daily loss limit would invert the comparison and make the kill switch fire immediately or never; out-of-range input clamps to 0.

nodes.label: paper.open subtracts cost and adds position
nodes.rationale: Opening must debit cash and append exactly one open position — the ledger the loss limit is measured against.
nodes.norm_label: paper.open subtracts cost and adds position

nodes.label: paper.close updates realizedToday
nodes.rationale: realizedToday is the input to the kill-switch comparison, so closing must post the realised P&L and flip the position status.

nodes.label: describe: generateStrategies — money math
nodes.rationale: Strategy generation across six band/spot configurations that each previously produced inverted legs, negative strikes or NaN money.

nodes.label: no NaN/undefined anywhere across six band configurations
nodes.rationale: A very wide band (10..190) used to produce a negative strike and then NaN cost/maxLoss; asserts finite cost, maxLoss, prob in [0,1], positive strikes and finite premium for every generated card.
nodes.norm_label: no nan/undefined anywhere across six band configurations

nodes.label: spread legs are ordered correctly for their structure
nodes.rationale: A band entirely below spot used to invert bull call legs and a band entirely above spot inverted bear put legs; pins long<short for debit call spreads, long>short for bear put spreads, Klp<Ksp<Ksc<Klc for condors, and that paired legs never collide on the same strike.
nodes.norm_label: spread legs are ordered correctly for their structure

nodes.label: long put max profit subtracts the premium paid
nodes.rationale: maxProfit was reported as K*100, ignoring the debit paid; correct value is (K - premium)*100 and must be strictly less than the old wrong figure.
nodes.norm_label: long put max profit subtracts the premium paid

nodes.label: maxProfit/maxLoss stay correct when strikes fall outside +/-50% of spot
nodes.rationale: A wide band (20..185) pushes condor wings far from spot and the old +/-50% payoff scan grid never sampled them, so extrema were computed from a truncated curve.
nodes.norm_label: maxprofit/maxloss stay correct when strikes fall outside +/-50% of spot
